recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Latvia sending about 20 soldiers to the Strait of Hormuz was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. This one was a genuine deployment, not a keyword-matching error like the wildfire correction below — but it's Latvia's own contribution to an international coalition maritime security mission on the other side of the world, with no connection to Russia or the Baltic region. The scoring gap that let this through (a Baltic country's own unrelated foreign deployments passing as a Baltic security signal) has been fixed. As always, the false positive stays in the historical record rather than being quietly deleted.
recent_corrections.context: Latvia plans to send about 20 soldiers to Strait of Hormuz — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-04

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Lithuania sending firefighters to help France fight wildfires was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. Cause: a scoring bug — generic words like 'deployed' and 'reinforcements' (meant to catch real troop movements) were also matching ordinary disaster-response language. That bug, and several similar ones found in a full audit of the scoring keywords, has been fixed. The false positive stays in the historical record below rather than being quietly deleted — see our policy on this.
recent_corrections.context: Lithuania sends 32 firefighters to help France fight wildfires — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-01

recent_updates.title: Fixed: alert maps were arriving stamped “API KEY REQUIRED”
recent_updates.text: The map service started requiring a paid key and began writing “API KEY REQUIRED” across every map sent with an alert. Nothing detected it, because a defaced tile arrives as a perfectly normal image. Maps now come from a different, free provider, and before each map the system checks a tile of open ocean — which should be blank — to confirm nothing is being stamped over it. If no provider is usable, the map is still sent with a plain grid rather than a defaced one. Thanks to the subscriber who reported it.

recent_updates.title: Browser alerts are retried, and failed delivery no longer goes unnoticed
recent_updates.text: If a browser push service was momentarily busy, that subscriber simply missed the alert — there was no retry, and the failure was only ever recorded in a log nobody reads. Delivery is now retried once, and if anyone still misses an alert the owner is told immediately how many did not receive it. Telegram delivery was never affected by this.

recent_updates.title: WARN can now actually fire when three newsrooms confirm the same thing
recent_updates.text: WARN had been reached once in 323 scans, and the reason turned out to be a flaw rather than quiet news: the rule needed sources of two different trust levels, but nearly all the newsroom feeds sit at the same level. So ERR, Postimees and LSM all confirming one drone incursion scored no higher than a single passing mention. Three independent newsrooms now count as confirmation on their own — while three outlets reprinting the same agency copy word-for-word still count as one. The description of WARN on this page was also promising something the code did not do, and has been corrected.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: the “feeds read directly” number on this page was hardcoded, not live
recent_updates.text: The page reads that count from the live data file, but the field was never actually being written to it, so it silently fell back to a number typed into the page. It happened to be correct until the count changed today. Now published properly, with a test that every number this page claims to read is really there.

recent_updates.title: Officials saying “we are coping” no longer arrive as alerts
recent_updates.text: A defence minister interview saying the country can respond to hybrid threats was sent as an alert, because the phrase “hybrid” was being treated as a reported incident. It is not — it is how commentators describe a situation. Terms like that now count towards relevance but no longer override the filters, which in turn made it safe to catch the wider class of officials reassuring the public that things are under control. Genuine incident reports are unaffected: they match on words like sabotage or drone incursion, which still override everything.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: a completed scan could be thrown away and leave this page stale
recent_updates.text: A scheduled scan ran cleanly and sent its alerts, then lost its results because another workflow was writing to the same files at the same moment — and because publishing to this page was tied to that bookkeeping step, the site quietly kept showing an older scan. All five workflows that write data now take turns properly, the save step can now resolve that kind of clash instead of failing, and publishing here no longer depends on it at all.

recent_updates.title: Four more newsrooms read directly (22 → 26)
recent_updates.text: TVNET, Postimees Estonian-language, Lrytas and The Baltic Times are now read straight from the publishers, adding about 110 more articles per scan and more redundancy if any one source goes down. Deliberately added only after local-language matching was fixed — before that, a Latvian or Lithuanian newsroom feed was mostly unreadable to the scorer. LRT, Lithuania's public broadcaster, publishes no working RSS feed and remains reachable only indirectly.

recent_updates.title: The Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian and Russian press is now readable to the monitor
recent_updates.text: Testing threat headlines in the local languages found none of them detected — and the cause was worse than a missing word list. These languages decline names, and the declined form is the everyday one: Lithuanian media writes “Lietuvos” and “Lietuvoje”, neither of which matched “Lietuva”. Same for city names like “Ādažos” and “Vilniuje”. Fixed, along with local terms for drones, GPS interference, sabotage, infrastructure explosions and the smuggling balloons that keep closing Vilnius airport. Since the local press reports a Baltic incident first, this was the largest blind spot in the system. No new false alarms on a live scan.

recent_updates.title: Closed 17 blind spots, including one that hid the word “mobilisation”
recent_updates.text: A deliberate hunt for things the monitor could NOT see found most real Baltic threat types missing. The worst: “mobilisation” in British spelling — which every Baltic English-language outlet uses — matched nothing at all. Nor did any Baltic city name, so “Drone sightings shut down Vilnius airport” was ignored for not saying “Lithuania”. Now covered, along with GPS/GNSS interference, airport drone and balloon closures, railway and depot explosions, recruited saboteurs, election interference, weaponised migration, Kaliningrad transit pressure and diplomatic expulsions. Tested against a live scan: two genuine incidents newly caught, nothing lost, no new false alarms.

recent_updates.title: Better diagnosis when something is flagged by mistake
recent_updates.text: Each flagged story now privately records which term caused it to match, so a false alarm can be traced and fixed instead of guessed at after the article has rolled off the feed. The terms themselves are never published — they would be a map for anyone wanting to word coverage so it slips past.

recent_updates.title: The site now shows what the filters held back
recent_updates.text: Every scan records the relevant items its filters chose not to alert on, and why. The site publishes a rolling 30-day count under the existing explainer, so the quiet can be checked rather than taken on trust. It is not published as a "precision" score — that would need a human verdict on every alert.

recent_updates.title: Fewer false alarms: announced exercises and translated duplicates
recent_updates.text: A NATO or Baltic exercise announced weeks in advance is no longer treated as a warning — one exercise (Namejs 2026) had been pushing four separate alerts. Headlines where someone denies an intention ("Putin called mobilisation rumours nonsense") no longer read as threats. And the same story published in English, Latvian and Russian now counts once instead of three times. All of these are still shown, clearly labelled as context.

recent_updates.title: New: faster early warning between full scans
recent_updates.text: The full 150-source sweep takes about 19 minutes, so it can only run six times a day -- meaning up to 9.5 hours could pass between looks. A new lightweight check now runs every 2 hours over the direct publisher feeds (ERR, LSM, Delfi, Postimees, Yle and others) and raises an early warning if something real appears. It stays completely silent otherwise.

recent_updates.title: Fewer, better alerts
recent_updates.text: Reviewing every alert ever sent found many were reassuring news ("officials say no attack is coming"), scenario/analysis pieces, or the same story repeating for days. Those are now shown as context instead of arriving as an alert. Replayed over the full history this removes about half the notifications while keeping every genuine incident.

recent_updates.title: New: direct publisher feeds for resilience
recent_updates.text: Until now every tracked source was reached through Google News, which has occasionally blocked the whole scan at once. The monitor now also reads 15 feeds straight from the publishers themselves -- ERR, LSM, Delfi, Postimees, Yle, Meduza and others -- so a Google outage no longer means a blind spot. They are also far faster to fetch.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: one source could trigger a WARN on its own
recent_updates.text: WARN is supposed to mean several independent sources report the same thing. A configuration quirk let a single organisation listed under two tiers score as its own corroboration. Confirmation is now counted per organisation, not per feed, so WARN means what it says.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: NATO training near Kaliningrad going uncaught
recent_updates.text: A real NATO exercise near Kaliningrad was not flagged because the relevance filter only matched the literal phrase "military exercise" -- most outlets actually write "drills"/"wargames"/"manoeuvres" instead. Added coverage for those terms (gated on military context where the bare word has an everyday meaning too), so this class of story is caught going forward.

recent_updates.title: New: power grid outages charted on the public site
recent_updates.text: The forced (unplanned) generation-unit outage data /gridoutage already fetches from ENTSO-E is now also recorded every scan and charted on the site -- a new "Power grid outages over time" trend alongside GPS-jamming, AIS, military aircraft, and thermal hotspots. Still informational only, same as /gridoutage always was.

recent_updates.title: New: weekly public summary on Mastodon/Bluesky/Discord
recent_updates.text: A once-a-week summary post (quiet/watch/warn counts, latest escalation index reading) to the public Mastodon/Bluesky/Discord accounts only -- deliberately never Telegram, since that channel's QUIET-suppression rule stays untouched. Keeps the public accounts visibly active during long quiet stretches.

recent_updates.title: New: AIS kinematic-anomaly detection
recent_updates.text: Flags a vessel whose two recorded AIS positions imply a physically impossible speed (a classic GPS-spoofing tell, though also possibly a transponder misreport) -- private chat only, informational, never part of scoring or public alerting. Deliberately does NOT flag a vessel simply not reappearing in a later scan, since AIS coverage is already a short, non-exhaustive window.

recent_updates.title: New: downloadable CSV history export
recent_updates.text: Two new downloads on the site: scan-level history (level, source counts per scan) and the Composite Escalation Index (deviation score per scan), as CSV, for anyone doing independent analysis of this project's own data.

recent_updates.title: New: Discord as a fifth public alert channel
recent_updates.text: WATCH/WARN and recovery alerts now also post to Discord via an incoming webhook -- same infrequent, Telegram-independent scope as Mastodon and Bluesky. Requires a free DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL once the owner sets one up.

recent_updates.title: New: /gridoutage -- Baltic power grid outage tracking via ENTSO-E
recent_updates.text: On-demand check for forced (unplanned) power-generation outages across Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania via the EU's official ENTSO-E Transparency Platform. Generation outages only for now, not transmission/interconnector lines -- a documented gap. Requires a free ENTSOE_API_KEY once registered.

recent_updates.title: Removed: /satellite (raw Sentinel-2 imagery)
recent_updates.text: Free Sentinel-2 imagery was too low-resolution to be genuinely useful, and higher-resolution commercial/SAR imagery is not affordable at this project's scale, so the feature was removed entirely.

recent_updates.title: New: /satellite change detection -- pixel differences, not AI verdicts
recent_updates.text: Owner-requested, deliberately scoped after weighing estwarden.eu's automated garrison-occupancy detection: /satellite now shows how much a site's imagery differs from the last clear shot, as a plain pixel-difference percentage. No object detection, no "occupied/empty" claims -- just the number, always caveated, never wired into scoring.

recent_updates.title: Signal Deviation Index: added a plain-language reading and a one-line why
recent_updates.text: The index now shows a band ("moderately elevated", "highest in N scans of tracking") instead of a bare percentage, plus a short sentence naming which signal actually moved. Same underlying numbers, easier to read at a glance.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: a flagged story could link straight to a Russian state-media site
recent_updates.text: GDELT-sourced items used their raw source URL as the public link, which could point directly at a Russian state-media/government domain -- untrustworthy for anyone tapping through from a browser notification. Now routed to a neutral page instead; the story is still tracked and cited by name.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: syndicated duplicates still showing in Recent flagged items
recent_updates.text: Same article text under different outlet names ("...- Inbox.lv" vs "...- LA.LV") wasn't caught by the earlier title dedup since the outlet suffix differed. Now strips it before comparing.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: raw NOTAM coordinates dumped into WATCH/WARN alerts
recent_updates.text: The auto-added NOTAM context could show up to 10 restricted-area listings with full coordinate lists in one alert -- unreadable to a civilian. Shortened to 3 short, coordinate-free lines with a pointer to /notam for full detail.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: Signal Deviation Index under-reported tracked sources
recent_updates.text: Showed "0 of 4 tracked" on days when 1 source genuinely had a baseline, just not the 2 needed for a composite reading. Now reports the true count.
